evidence: A carbon budget for fruit on the whole-plant model's stand over the lunar cycle (plant.py: the canopy model's photosynthesis with twilight, leaf and stem-and-root respiration, at the chosen climate's land air temperatures). One watermelon-like fruit cohort is set per cycle and develops in degree-days above 10 C (560 from set to harvest, from growers' 35-45 days at about a 24 C mean), with its potential dry mass on a beta sigmoid peaking at half the development (checked against a third of the harvest weight 15 days after set; Noh et al. 2013): 7.5 kg fresh, 8.6% dry matter, 42% carbon (USDA composition), growth respiration of a quarter and maintenance of 0.01 g CH2O per g dry matter per day at 25 C (Q10 = 2). Development is taken to follow temperature alone, and the fruit sets whenever it is pollinated. Flowering, fruit set and abortion, seeds, water, fruit quality and the crop's own canopy (the stand is plant.py's leaf area index 5) are not modelled.
reading_rule: Carbon is g C per m2 of ground per solar cycle; a load is fruits set per m2 per cycle, one cohort per cycle, so a fruit that takes longer than a cycle overlaps the next. Hour angles are degrees from local noon (-90 sunrise, 90 sunset). results[side][band][strategy] (strategies as in plant.json): set_times gives, for each set hour angle, the days to harvest, the harvest hour angle, the nights the fruit lives through, the share of its potential growth that falls while the plant is in deficit (growth_while_plant_short), and at the reference load (fruit carbon half the plant's growth without fruit) the store and the plant's remaining growth when the fruit is fed throughout (fed) and the fruit's size as a share of its potential when it grows only on the daylight surplus (daylight). best is the set time with the Sun up that needs the smallest store (fed) or grows the largest fruit (daylight), with loads swept from none upward and interpolated to fruit shares of new tissue carbon (shares). harvest_kg is fresh fruit per m2 per cycle; plant_growth the plant's own new tissue; canopy_cycles the cycles that growth would take to build a whole new canopy (211.5 g C). calendar gives the degree-days of the sunlit half and the cycle and the fruit-zone temperature needed to ripen within one sunlit half. earth is the same stand and fruit under Earth's sky with the same temperatures over 24 hours, with harvests per 29.53 days. sensitivity varies one setting at a time at the equatorial near side, Earth-like plant.

units.carbon: g C m-2 of ground per solar cycle
units.harvest: kg fresh fruit m-2 per cycle

sources.harvest_mass: Noh et al. 2013, Physiol. Mol. Biol. Plants 19:509-514: 7.1-8.3 kg per plant at harvest and 2.3-3.0 kg 15 days after fruit set (Sambok-gul, Korea)
sources.composition: USDA FoodData Central 167765, watermelon, raw: 91.4 g water, 7.55 g carbohydrate, 0.61 g protein, 0.15 g fat per 100 g
sources.development: a seed company's cultivation guide (Origene Seeds): 35-45 days from fruit set to maturity with 25-35 C days and 15-20 C nights; ripe (red flesh) 36 days after pollination in the field at Lane, Oklahoma (Wechter et al. 2008, BMC Genomics 9:275)
sources.thresholds: watermelon base temperatures of 10-12.7 C and an upper threshold of 37 C (review of growing-degree-day thresholds, Agricultural Water Management 2025)
sources.growth_curve: Yin et al. 2003, Annals of Botany 91:361-371 (beta sigmoid)
sources.maintenance: WOFOST system description: typical maintenance coefficients 0.03 (leaves), 0.015 (stems), 0.01 (roots) g CH2O per g per day at 25 C (Spitters et al. 1989), 0.01 for organs other than leaves in tropical crops (Penning de Vries et al. 1989)
